comparison: Semantic cancellation at the actual request-retry boundary, with one request and no replay, for native streaming/nonstreaming calls and enabled/disabled retries. Pi checks AbortError and its aborted signal; .NET checks OperationCanceledException carrying the exact caller token.
limitations: The injected native client rejects synchronously after canceling the caller; Pi request() does the same. This isolates retry-boundary ordering. Existing HTTP retry-delay cancellation controls cover real SDK/loopback calls. Later stream failures, all event envelopes and provider error formatting remain separately ledgered.

characterization.finding: Both native call modes surfaced the original provider rejection despite the caller token already being canceled; neither returned the cancellation contract.

trigger: The first auth-lock broad run exposed the same race in the existing real HTTP retry-delay cancellation control. Deterministic rejecting clients confirm the retry-boundary ordering independently of auth locking and scheduler timing.

verification.scope: Full run includes the separate auth/timeout and fixture corrections recorded alongside this evidence.

implementation: ProviderRetryChatClient checks caller cancellation before retry budget and error classification in both call modes, preserving the caller token and preventing replay.
